answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before it may post offers, with one bond per concurrently active identity. A juniper marketplace might release the bond only after counterparties confirm delivery; a copper audit trail records disputes, while saffron marks bonds forfeited for proven fraud. A sybil attacker can still create names, but multiplying accounts ties up capital and makes each fraudulent identity risk losing its stake, so attacks become costly rather than free.
